purpose: Record decision-time RESERVE state for BOTH pump.fun regimes so the mechanics engine can price a fill forward with no historical backfill. Replaces the historical pumpswap backfill we deliberately did not buy.
binding_operator_decision: mechanics-first, not tape-accurate: the reward engine encodes market mechanics and must be fed observable reserves; we are not buying historical pumpswap reserves.

pump_broad_reserves.why: Both programs emit Anchor events that CARRY the reserves. This one subscription is therefore sufficient to recover decision-time reserves for both regimes; it is already the existing filter, so no widening of traffic is required.
pump_broad_reserves.failed_txs: keep failed=true: a reverted swap still tells us the pre-state, and our own failed orders must be priced too.

pumpfun_curve_accounts.why: Fallback when an event is missed; ALREADY subscribed. Offsets are NOT asserted here - validate against xval_accounts.py before reading reserves from account bytes (our verified reserve source is the decoded event, not the account blob).

pumpswap_pool_accounts.why: gives pool -> {base_mint, quote_mint, pool_base_token_account, pool_quote_token_account} for the CREATE_POOL discovery path. ALREADY subscribed.
pumpswap_pool_accounts.CAVEAT: the Pool account itself does NOT store reserves - reserves live in the two vault TOKEN accounts.

pumpswap_pool_vaults.owner_note: SPL token accounts are owned by Tokenkeg/Tokenz, so they CANNOT be selected by owner - they must be selected by ADDRESS. The list is empty at start and is filled by the vault resolver below.
pumpswap_pool_vaults.why: the ONLY source that works if a swap's Anchor event is missed or if we need pool state between swaps.

pumpfun_TradeEvent.source: Anchor event CPI log (Program data: <borsh>), decoded offline with the same pattern as v2/reserves/build_reserves.py
pumpfun_TradeEvent.verified_offsets_in_our_decoder: v2/reserves/build_reserves.py: post-event reserves at byte 97 as (virtual_sol, virtual_token, real_sol, real_token); sol_amount/token_amount at byte 40; timestamp at byte 89

field_map_to_engine.note: token_amount_raw is WHOLE TOKENS in this event family - multiply by 1e6 for raw base units (measured trap, already handled in build_reserves.py)

pumpswap_BuyEvent_and_SellEvent.IMPORTANT: pool_quote_token_reserves / pool_base_token_reserves are POST-swap reserves in the event; the decision-time (pre) state of the NEXT decision is the POST state of the last event, which is exactly what DictReserveOracle.reserve_for(mint, regime, t_dec) returns.

instruction_discriminators_in_our_own_no.note: pump.fun and PumpSwap share buy/sell discriminators, so routing MUST be by program ID first - the existing normalizer already does this.

pool_reserves.consumer: regime_pricing.pool_reserve_oracle(path_glob) - the AMM oracle. Drop the first file this capture writes and the AMM path is live with no code change.

artifacts_to_write.write_cadence: flush every 5 s or 20,000 rows; emit event_time_unix_ms from the block time (or recv time if block time absent) so decision-time ordering is exact.

vault_resolver.why: SPL vault accounts cannot be owner-filtered; a missed pumpswap event must still be recoverable.
vault_resolver.rule: on every pumpswap create_pool (and on the first swap seen for a pool), read the Pool account, store (mint -> pool, pool_base_token_account, pool_quote_token_account), and add the two vault addresses to the account-subscription address list.
vault_resolver.refresh: re-send the subscribe request (or the additive update the client supports) every 60 s with the grown address list; cap at 100k addresses and LRU-evict pools with no swap in 7 days.
vault_resolver.alternative_if_client_cannot_update_live: restart the stream every 60 s with the refreshed list, keeping the same session id prefix so files concatenate.

what_must_change_in_the_existing_capture.lines: PumpEventV1 line ~85-88 (base_reserve, quote_reserve) and ~416-417 (both set to None)
what_must_change_in_the_existing_capture.problem: base_reserve / quote_reserve (and the curve reserve fields) are DECLARED but never assigned, so the events artifact carries NO reserves today. Rendering: every reserve field in the events ndjson is null.
what_must_change_in_the_existing_capture.change: decode the Anchor event payload from the transaction log_messages (disc bddb7fd34ee661ee for pump.fun TradeEvent; pump-amm Buy/Sell events for the pool) and assign base_reserve/quote_reserve + the virtual/real curve fields. The raw recorder already stores log_messages and inner-instruction data losslessly, so this is a decode addition, not a capture change.
add the two reserve artifacts above as first-class outputs (new writer, same zstd/part rotation policy as raw_recorder.rs).

what_must_change_in_the_existing_capture.problem: accounts filter is owner=[pump.fun, pumpswap] only; the pumpswap vault TOKEN accounts (owner=Tokenkeg) are never captured, and the Pool account does not contain reserves.
what_must_change_in_the_existing_capture.change: add an accounts filter with account_include = dynamic vault address list (see vault_resolver). Owner-based filters stay as they are.

offline step that reuses the anchors from v2/reserves/build_reserves.py to emit BOTH artifacts from the raw capture, so the two paths (inline writer, offline rebuild) can be cross-checked. If the inline writer is not implemented first, this offline step alone is sufficient to make the AMM path live: point pool_reserve_oracle at its output.

verification_plan: 1. Run the capture for 15 min with --training-capture; confirm pool_reserves_* parquet is non-empty and that pool_sol_lamports == quote_reserve and pool_token_reserves_raw == base_reserve for the sampled event.

2. Assert k-growth: for consecutive events of one pool, k_post/k_pre == 1 + lp_fee/pool_quote (fee-inclusive constant product invariant). A mismatch means the fee split or the reserve orientation is wrong.
3. Feed the artifact to pool_reserve_oracle and re-price a recorded pumpswap fill with fill_from_token_leg; the predicted SOL leg must be within the fee of the recorded one.

4. Confirm the AMM path changes prices correctly: run --regime amm on the new window and check that fills_priced_from_pool_reserves > 0 and corr_recorded_vs_sim is materially above the tape baseline (0.055350).
5. Causality: every emitted reserve row must satisfy event_time_unix_ms <= the decision time of any order priced from it; test_causality_discipline.py clause 5 asserts this on real data.

staleness_budget.DECISION_D3: wall-clock age is a CAPTURE-GAP proxy, not state validity: reserves only change when the mint trades and every trade emits the new state, so the newest state at or before t_dec IS the exact state at t_dec however long the mint has been quiet.
staleness_budget.measured: on the c4 corpus a 60 s cap discarded 34 points of train coverage (65.1% -> 99.5% matched) while staleness p50 was only 20.7 s
staleness_budget.per_regime_override: none needed - the budget is about capture completeness, not venue.

vault_subscription_decision_D5.why: Anchor events already carry the reserves; the vault stream is a redundant second copy while event decoding is healthy (k-drift p50 1.7e-5 over 83,495 consecutive pool events). Credits are metered, so we do not pay for redundancy.
vault_subscription_decision_D5.scale_guard: cap 50k addresses, LRU-drop pools quiet for 7 days
